1.explanation: Both of these files implement Prettier’s Angular‐template embed logic for interpolation (`{{ … }}`) and for attribute bindings (`[attr]="…"` or bare attributes) respectively. They parse out the pipe expressions and then build a Doc to print the `|` and `:` tokens. The unwanted spaces around `:` originate in these two plugins when they hard-code or infer a space before and after every colon. To restore the legacy behavior for literal args, you would update the colon-printing logic in these files to skip inserting spaces when the argument node is a string or numeric literal, and only leave in spaces in the other cases per the compromise proposal.

2.explanation:
These four files form the end-to-end pipeline for Angular pipe formatting:

• src/language-html/embed/angular-interpolation.js
  – Detects “{{…}}” interpolation in HTML and hands the inner expression to the Angular‐aware parser.

• src/language-js/parse/angular.js
  – The Angular parsing plugin that recognizes pipe expressions and colon separators, building a special AST node for them.

• src/plugins/angular.js
  – Registers the Angular parser plugin with Prettier’s core, so that pipe expressions are routed through the above parser.

• src/language-js/print/html-binding.js
  – The printer for Angular bindings which currently emits spaces around every colon; this is where you would adjust spacing rules (omit spaces when the argument node is a literal string or number, but keep them in other cases).
